findings.label: Paid During Active Breaches
findings.detail: 5 suppliers received payments while in breach of Companies Act — including 0 critical and 0 high severity. Temporally verified against payment dates.

findings.label: Likely Duplicate Payments
findings.detail: 499 high-confidence duplicate groups with same supplier, amount, date and reference (3+ copies) (after filtering 46502 CSV republication artifacts)
findings.context_note: Quarterly CSV overlaps (same transaction appearing in 2 files) have been filtered out. Remaining duplicates show 3+ identical copies, which are more likely genuine overpayments.

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 353 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 1596 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Vcare-24 Ltd (2.0 day avg, 24 payments, £15.9K)

findings.label: Benford's Law Anomaly
findings.detail: Significant deviation from Benford's Law (p < 0.001). Digit 1 deviates 17.9% from expected distribution across 443,560 transactions. Note: with 443,560 transactions, chi-squared tests are highly sensitive — the 17.9% max digit deviation is the more practical measure of anomaly.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 443,560+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (17.9%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 443,560 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 8 deviates 2.31% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=443,560.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 43 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: Big Picture Learning - Social Impact Bond (£6.5M)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

findings.label: High-Risk Councillors
findings.detail: 19 councillors scored 'high risk' in integrity assessment across 36 data sources. Most common flags: undeclared interests, supplier conflicts, and company compliance issues.

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Vcare-24 Ltd — every 2.0 days (24 payments, £15.9K)

key_findings.title: LIVING AMBITIONS LTD: 39065 transactions totalling £31.2M
key_findings.description: Averaging £798 per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: 31 suppliers shared with neighbouring councils — £218.4M total
key_findings.description: Compare what each council pays the same suppliers for similar services

key_findings.title: EE LTD: 7876% price gap between councils
key_findings.description: Derbyshire_Cc pays £11.0K avg vs Hyndburn £138 (both with 3+ transactions). Price differences may reflect different service scope, contract terms, or volumes rather than overcharging — manual review recommended.
key_findings.context_note: Cross-council price comparisons use common financial years only (where both councils have data for the same supplier). This prevents unfair comparisons between councils with different data periods. Differences may still reflect different service levels or contract terms.

key_findings.title: 2 service categories with a single supplier
key_findings.description: Top: Iveco ltd — sole winner in 'Cranes, mobile lifting frames and works ' (2 contracts, £388.8K). Category monopolies may indicate market failure or specification bias.

key_findings.title: AI DOGE covers 61% of £535.0M GOV.UK outturn
key_findings.description: Spending >£500 threshold means smaller transactions are excluded. Largest gaps: Education services, Highways and transport services, Children Social Care. This is expected — not a data quality issue.
